description: The Windows quad finder (ADR-R48 Windows, W4) on drawn grey frames, and line boxes plus quads through FrameScreens.detect. Generated by tools/fixtures/clip-frames/generate_frame_quads.py; C# FrameQuadVectorTests replays every case.

frames.note: The Mac's drawn phone screen, at its place, words as bars, 3x3 blurred.
The same phone turned about 2.86 degrees about its centre.
A laptop lid in slight perspective, on a wall gradient, its keyboard deck touching the lid.
No rectangle: a face-like ellipse, eyes, mouth and shoulders on soft gradients.
One rectangle among circles, triangles, lines, small squares and kites.
A rectangle too small (short side 30 px < 36) and one large enough (44 px).
A rectangle too thin (48/200 = 0.24) and one wide enough (56/160 = 0.35).
A parallelogram 32.1 degrees off square and one 14.8 degrees off.
A rectangle whose top and bottom fade (edges on two sides only) and a sharp twin.
Eight rounded rectangles, corner radii [16, 0, 36, 8, 4, 30, 12, 20] px: the six squarest are kept.

quads.note: The lid and its screen; the deck is skewed past 25 degrees.
An ellipse fills pi/4 of the quad around it; gradients have no edges.
minimumConfidence 0.6: two sides of four is 0.5.

scans.note: The drawn phone's six lines with the finder's quads: framed screens with a rectangle source.
The same six lines with no rectangle source: under the 8-box cluster rule, so no screen.
Lines on the no-rectangle frame: no quad, so only a cluster could be a screen.
3 lines are a screen only because a quad holds them.
The same 3 lines without the quad.
5 lines are a screen only because a quad holds them.
The same 5 lines without the quad.
7 lines are a screen only because a quad holds them.
The same 7 lines without the quad.
Three lines covering under 4 % of the quad.
Lines beside the quad, not in it.
Eight lines with no quad: a dense-text cluster, not framed.
A framed screen and a cluster in one frame.
